title: KV cache tiling, temporal slack reservoirs, and allocation simulator
creator: Elena Morales
description: Design and implement a KV cache allocation strategy and operational playbook that reduces long-running GPU memory fragmentation while preserving continuous batching latency and throughput. Deliver a lightweight allocation simulator and telemetry surface that lets runtime engineers predict fragmentation under realistic workload traces and evaluate mitigation knobs before rolling to production.
background: We observe incremental KV cache fragmentation over extended uptimes on high-throughput workloads. Fragmentation increases peak memory pressure and forces conservative soft-reserves or cold-start drops. Existing approaches (slab-based, region compaction) either add CPU overhead or disrupt latency-sensitive continuous batching windows. We need an approach that reduces fragmentation without hurting tail-latency or increasing per-request jitter.
goals: 1) Reduce long-term fragmentation measured as unusable bytes across multiple sequence-length distributions. 2) Keep p95/p99 generation latency within 5% of baseline. 3) Add operational visibility and a safe rollout path for live workloads.
proposal: Introduce three coordinated pieces: (A) cache-tiling allocation: partition the KV pool into independently-managed tiles keyed by token-length bucket and affinity (short/medium/long). Tiles use slot pools optimized for their expected allocation size distribution to avoid inter-size internal fragmentation; (B) temporal slack reservoirs: small overprovisioned buffers per tile that absorb transient allocation spikes and reduce churn-driven fragmentation; (C) offline allocation simulator and fragment estimator: a trace-driven simulator modeled on runtime allocation events that reports projected fragmentation, peak reservation needs, and recommends tile boundaries and slack sizes. Additionally, expose new telemetry (per-tile occupancy histograms, relocation events, compaction throughput) and a background coalescer that performs epochal, bandwidth-limited defragmentation aligned to low-batch windows.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end simulator can ingest real traces (JSON trace format) and produce fragmentation forecast reports within 30s for a 24h trace.
End-to-end fragmentation (usable vs. total bytes) improves by >=20% on benchmark traces compared to current slab baseline, with no >5% regression in p99 latency under production-like batching.
New telemetry surfaces are available in Console: per-tile occupancy, relocation count, coalescer activity, and a fragmentation scorecard.
Background coalescer can be enabled with an opt-in runtime flag and performs controlled relocations without increasing request tail-latency beyond regression threshold.
Runbook and rollout doc in Drive with clear canary steps and abort criteria.
Unit and integration tests for allocator invariants and simulator parity checks added to CI.
success_metrics: Relative fragmentation reduction on target traces (percent), p95/p99 latency regression (ms and percent), number of relocation events per hour, memory headroom reclaimed (MB), and number of rollbacks triggered during canary.

implementation_notes: Allocator changes live in gpu_kv_manager. Key components: (1) Tile manager that maps incoming allocation requests to tile based on request metadata and token-length hint; (2) Per-tile slab/slot pools with small-power-of-two slab sizing + a hot-evict ring for short-lived objects; (3) Temporal slack reservoir implemented as a soft-allocated freelist with a time-based decay policy to release slack back to global pool; (4) Background coalescer that coalesces adjacent free slots with a bandwidth cap to avoid blocking batch processing; (5) Simulator reuses existing trace ingestion code in tools/alloc-sim and emits a CSV/HTML report. Keep allocator fast-path mostly unchanged: tile mapping is a simple table lookup; heavy operations run in background threads scheduled by the runtime orchestration.
telemetry_and_metrics: New metrics: kv.tile.occupancy_bytes, kv.tile.free_slots, kv.tile.relocations_total, kv.coalescer.throughput_bytes_s, kv.fragmentation_score (0-100), kv.simulator.estimated_fragmentation. Add heatmap export for tile occupancy and a ‘fragmentation alert’ threshold for Console alerts.
testing_plan: 1) Unit tests for tile mapping logic and slack reservoir decay. 2) Replay tests using recorded production traces against simulator and allocator prototype to validate parity. 3) Perf harness: run generation workloads (short-only, long-only, mixed) measuring latency and fragmentation over 24h. 4) Canary: enable flag for 1% traffic on a dedicated Dedicated pool, monitor fragmentation and tail latency for 48h.
rollout_plan: Feature behind runtime flag. Staged rollout: internal infra nodes -> 1% customer dedicated pools -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%. Abort criteria: fragmentation increases by >5% versus baseline or p99 latency regression >5% for 30m window.
risks:
- Tile misclassification for multi-length requests could increase cross-tile copying. Mitigation: conservative mapping heuristics and a fallback to global pool.
- Background coalescer may interfere with GPU memory allocator if not bandwidth-limited. Mitigation: rate limit coalescer and run during low-batch windows.
- Simulator fidelity mismatch causing bad recommendations. Mitigation: validate simulator against short offline replays and instrument parity checks.
